prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1090; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver reporting a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. Claimant states she was stopped in the left-turn lane when the other vehicle crossed the center line. Reported knee pain at the scene and declined ambulance transport. Vehicle damage described as front bumper and hood on both vehicles. Police report number requested.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant to confirm the account of the collision. She reports her right knee struck the lower dashboard on impact and has been swollen since. She has not retained an attorney and is handling the claim directly. Explained the medical payments coverage available under her policy and advised her to keep all receipts and treatment records.

Entry 3: Received the responding officer's report. It notes both drivers were cooperative, no citations were issued, and the other driver admitted to drifting toward the center lane while distracted. Photos of both vehicles attached to the file. Liability appears clear and is being reviewed against the statement from the other driver.

Entry 4: Claimant submitted an initial medical record from an urgent care visit showing a sprain of the right knee with limited range of motion. Physician recommended physical therapy and a follow-up in two weeks. Requested the complete treatment file and an itemized bill. Advised claimant that we will need her authorization to obtain records directly from the provider.

Entry 5: Claimant called to ask about the status of her medical payments claim and whether she should expect a rental reimbursement. Confirmed the medical claim is pending receipt of the itemized bill and the physical therapy notes. Rental coverage is active under her policy, and reimbursement will be processed once the receipts are submitted. Scheduled a follow-up call after the records are received.
